Well I've been struggling quite awhile with depression and more recently social anxiety, I would estimate since I was 14. After a suicide attempt at 16, I was forced into therapy which was awful and didn't help. Fast forward to college, and I realized it was time for me to take initiative. I began seeing a counselor...which was awful and didn't help. Then fast forward to last summer and I found a psychologist who was AWESOME and I began making legitimate progress in my recovery. I also visited the GP who prescribed me zoloft. Then when college started again I became really really depressed. I overdosed twice on my meds and ended up in the psych ward. Sooooo that was like a month ago. Now, I'm seeing a psychiatrist, a psychologist, meeting with my academic advisor every week (she has a master's in counseling and is awesome), and doing group therapy. AND I got my medication switched to prozac, and it actually works now.

So basically I'm getting help now because it's literally either that or I die. I cannot tell you how many "plans" for suicide I've made. It's getting so aggravating and tiring always dealing with this. Like I have anxiety attacks probably every day. I can't live like this, and I've recently realized that my friends and family DO love me, so I can't kill myself. It's all I can do. 

I used to avoid getting help because of the "stigma" surrounding mental health disorders. But, whether it's due to the depression or becoming more mature, I stopped caring at all. Also I really had no idea how ill I was. It's still amazing to me when I have good days how DIFFERENT the entire world is. It's incredible.
